project: Prove Live Runtime-Backed Factory Session Status and Result Through `you mcp serve`
description: Add one documented runtime-backed `you mcp serve` mode that reuses the existing Factory Session MCP tools against the shared durable JavaScript runtime service, prove one focused async start/status/result smoke path through stdio MCP serve, and keep the existing fixture-backed serve smoke as the default additive path.

context.customerAsk: Document and prove a runtime-backed `you mcp serve` mode that exposes the existing Factory Session MCP tools against the shared durable JavaScript backend, with focused smoke coverage for async start, status polling, and result retrieval.
context.problem: The current stdio MCP serve path is tied to the deterministic durable session fixture catalog. Hosts can discover tools and exercise fixture-backed async behavior, but they cannot yet prove that the same MCP surface works against the shared live durable runtime service without widening into HTTP/SSE transport, dashboard inspection, or a broader MCP redesign.
context.solution: Add one explicit serve-mode selection for `you mcp serve` so operators can opt into the shared runtime-backed durable execution service while preserving the existing default fixture-backed mode. Reuse the existing Factory Session MCP catalog and shared runtime service, document the runtime mode in the MCP docs, and add one smoke path that starts an async JavaScript Factory Session, polls status, and reads a not-ready or terminal result through the runtime mode.

acceptanceCriteria: `you mcp serve` offers one documented runtime-backed mode that selects the shared durable JavaScript runtime service while preserving the existing default fixture-backed mode

In runtime-backed mode, the existing `you.factory_session.*` MCP tools can start one async Factory Session, poll session status, and read a not-ready or terminal result through the shared durable runtime path
The Factory Session MCP catalog, public vocabulary, and tool ownership remain under the existing `pkg/mcp/factorysession` registry with no MCP-only session model or duplicate session logic
Focused smoke coverage proves one runtime-backed stdio host path for async start, status polling, and result retrieval without requiring unrelated API or website changes
Existing fixture-backed `you mcp serve` smoke continues to pass, proving the runtime-backed serve path is additive rather than a replacement
Scope remains explicitly bounded to live runtime-backed stdio MCP serve and does not widen into website inspection, HTTP/SSE transport, or a broad CLI/API/event parity sweep
Typecheck, lint, and focused tests pass for the changed CLI, MCP, runtime, and documentation surfaces

userStories.title: Select runtime-backed MCP serve mode
userStories.description: As an operator configuring an MCP host, I want one explicit way to start `you mcp serve` against the shared runtime-backed execution service so that I can use the existing Factory Session MCP tools with live durable JavaScript execution.
acceptanceCriteria: `you mcp serve` supports one documented runtime-backed mode in addition to the existing default fixture-backed mode
The runtime-backed mode selects the shared `factorysessionexecution.RuntimeService` rather than a fixture catalog
The default `you mcp serve` behavior remains fixture-backed unless the runtime-backed mode is explicitly selected
Runtime mode selection does not rename or remove the existing `you.factory_session.*` tools
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Expose live async Factory Session behavior through existing MCP tools
userStories.description: As an MCP host using the Factory Session catalog, I want `you.factory_session.start_async`, `you.factory_session.get`, and `you.factory_session.get_result` to operate against the shared durable runtime service so that live session execution can be observed through the documented stdio MCP surface.
acceptanceCriteria: In runtime-backed mode, `you.factory_session.start_async` can start one durable JavaScript Factory Session through the shared runtime service
`you.factory_session.get` returns observable status updates for that live session, including a non-terminal status while work is still running when the scenario reaches that state
`you.factory_session.get_result` returns the existing not-ready behavior while the session is incomplete and returns the terminal result once the session finishes
The live MCP path reuses the existing Factory Session tool registry and shared durable execution service instead of duplicating session lifecycle logic inside the MCP layer
Public vocabulary remains Factory Session, Dispatch, Provider Session, and artifact oriented
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Prove one focused runtime-backed MCP smoke path
userStories.description: As a maintainer shipping MCP host support, I want one focused smoke test for runtime-backed `you mcp serve` so that the live stdio serve mode is proven without requiring a broader host or transport matrix.
acceptanceCriteria: Focused smoke coverage spawns `you mcp serve` in runtime-backed mode and discovers the existing Factory Session MCP catalog
The smoke flow starts one async JavaScript Factory Session through `you.factory_session.start_async`
The smoke flow polls the same session through `you.factory_session.get` until it observes either a non-terminal status plus not-ready result or terminal completion plus terminal result
The smoke flow reads the result through `you.factory_session.get_result` and proves the runtime-backed serve mode is using the shared durable backend rather than the fixture catalog
Smoke coverage stays focused on stdio MCP serve behavior and does not require unrelated API, SSE, or dashboard assertions
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Preserve additive fixture coverage and document the scope boundary
userStories.description: As a maintainer extending MCP install proof, I want the existing fixture-backed smoke path and customer documentation to remain valid so that the runtime-backed serve lane is additive and its scope stays explicit.
acceptanceCriteria: Existing fixture-backed `you mcp serve` smoke continues to pass without being rewritten to depend on the live runtime-backed mode
Customer-facing MCP documentation describes when to use the default fixture-backed mode versus the runtime-backed mode and how the runtime mode fits the stdio host setup
Documentation keeps Factory Session vocabulary and does not introduce a separate MCP-only session concept
Documentation explicitly records that this lane proves live runtime-backed stdio MCP serve only and defers website inspection, HTTP/SSE transport, and broader host-matrix expansion
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
